question: A plane interface separates air and a transparent medium of refractive index $n$ (with respect to air). A student proposes the hypothesis: Hypothesis: “For any transparent medium with $n>1$, the Brewster angle $i_p$ always lies strictly between $45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$.” Using Brewster’s law $\tan i_p = n$ (for light incident from air), analyze the hypothesis and choose the correct option that (i) converts $45^\circ1$, including one numerical counterexample if it is not.

options.A: Valid for all $n>1$, because $\tan i_p=n$ automatically gives $45^\circ<i_p<60^\circ$ for any $n>1$.
options.B: Not valid for all $n>1$. Since $45^\circ<i_p<60^\circ\iff \tan45^\circ<n<\tan60^\circ\iff 1<n<\sqrt{3}$, the hypothesis holds only for $1<n<\sqrt{3}$. Counterexample: $n=2\Rightarrow i_p=\tan^{-1}(2)\approx 63.4^\circ>60^\circ$.
options.C: Not valid. The condition $45^\circ<i_p<60^\circ$ holds only for $n>\sqrt{3}$; otherwise $i_p<45^\circ$. Counterexample: $n=1.2$ gives $i_p\approx 50^\circ$.
options.D: Valid only for $n>2$, because larger $n$ forces $i_p$ to stay between $45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. Counterexample: $n=1.5\Rightarrow i_p\approx 56.3^\circ$.
